obligations.obligation: must_include: Preparation movement rendered in scene (not summary): the carters' lore, Karis's derivation of the discharge-sense and the water-masking, Seln's cut-dog geometry, Cael's bait-with-one-declaration plan. Karis's finding is hers, stated as hypothesis before the fight and confirmed by it.
obligations.evidence: Carters' lore in scene, from the gate-woman: '"Dusk," she said. "Never noon. Noon you cross and they let you. Dusk they come out of the water." ... "The first man lit something at them when the mule went ... and that's the one we buried in pieces. The second didn't light anything ... The third didn't come up. Seven, the ferryman's boy said, or eight."' Seln's geometry, flat: '"A pack has a shape. There's one on the road every time. Whoever's holding the crossing, there's a dog behind him, cutting the way back, and it's never the one you're looking at. You'll be looking at the bar."' Karis's hypothesis, labeled as such in her method register: '"I want to say something, and I want it written that it's a hypothesis. Not a finding." ... "They don't hunt bodies. A still body is nearly nothing to them. They hunt *discharge* — what a Path does when it's used." ... "If discharge is what they sense, then water masks discharge. Ours and theirs. ... The river hides *them*. That's why the ford is theirs." ... "Hypothesis. Evidence for: everything. Evidence against: none, which I don't trust. Test: dusk."' Cael's plan: '"They hunt the declaration. So we give them one. One. Karis, on the bar, one point, once — and then nothing, from anyone, for the rest of the night. ... We bait with one declaration and kill with everything that isn't one."' Confirmation by the fight, in the log: '*Karis's hypothesis is a finding now. They hunt discharge. A still body is nearly nothing to them and a declaration is everything, and they turn to the loudest one, all seven, at once. Water hides them.*'

obligations.obligation: must_include: Terrain first and load-bearing — knee-deep water over slick stone, the mid-river gravel bar, the bank's scrub at forty meters, the current pulling downstream; at least two beats CAUSED by terrain (the submerged stone Brom planted on; the hounds hidden in the river; the bar Lira runs).
obligations.evidence: Terrain catalogued before the fight: 'Sixty paces wide, brown, moving right to left — downstream on his left as he faced it. ... a shingle flat, pale, bare, forty meters of it before the scrub began ... The ford was a sill of flat stone under the current — knee-deep, he learned by wading it, slimed green so that a boot went where the river wanted and not where the foot did. Twenty paces of that to a gravel bar in mid-river, long and low, thirty paces by eight, its stones dry and loose and rounded, the only thing on the river a person could run on.' Terrain-caused beat 1 (stone + current): 'its hind feet went out from under it on the slimed stone because there was nothing under them a foot could set, and the current took the hind end and turned the animal broadside, and Brom, planted on a stone he had found on purpose with a lip against its upstream side, put his shoulder down and through it and drove it under. It went with the current and did not come back.' Terrain-caused beat 2 (the river as the pack's cover): 'The river stood up. Seven places. Upstream, four grey backs broke the flat of the pool at once, without splash ... downstream, three.' Terrain-caused beat 3 (the bar): 'the gravel rolled under her right foot at speed — loose, rounded, dry, the only running ground on the river and the worst — and the ankle went over, all the way'.

Brom on his stone in the near channel, four paces short of the bar's near end, the current on his left ... Cael on the near shingle at the water's edge, twelve paces downstream of where the road went in'. FIRST (cut behind Brom, Iron Skin as declaration, the stone and current): 'The one came out of the downstream pool behind Brom, between Brom and the near shingle, in the road's own line' / 'Seven heads turned. Every dog on the river turned its face to the man who had just declared' / 'Brom saw it, and the amplification went off him like a coat. He was still large.' SECOND (Lira on the bar, no burst): 'for the first time since she was fourteen there was no burst at the end of it ... because she was, it turned out, fast. Fast without it.' THIRD (adaptation, convergence on Karis, the fear, the lattice not lit): 'the five that were left stopped testing the silent bodies. They turned, together ... toward the one thing on the river still making a noise on purpose.' / 'Karis did not light.' / 'Karis made a sound then that was not the stone. It was the only sound she made all night that was not on purpose.' FOURTH (first-mover finding, Cael's burst away from Karis, Seln behind the leader): 'The pack broke toward whichever hound moved first. So he moved first.' / 'downstream along the near shingle, away from the bar, away from Karis' / 'The water rose behind the grey in the shape of a man, and the grey went down'. Pauses are placed by channel, bar end, and pace counts throughout ('three paces off', 'a body's length off', 'chest-deep in the far channel at the bar's downstream tip').

inventions: The board beat: Teague's crew leaves for the autumn-road walk (the sixty-mark HOLD from Chapter 2) at first light on the fiftieth day; the Thornwater carter arrives empty with word of a third carter killed at the ford four days earlier; the hold releases the HOLD to 'whoever's standing at the board'; Pike strikes Teague's name with a single line and writes the five names in the margin, keeps the hold's forty marks, and states his reservation in his own register ('That's arithmetic I can't do yet.').

Thornwater's ford, within the allowed set: a sixty-pace river below the steading's east fence reached by a long grass fall; open shingle forty meters wide on both banks before the scrub; a knee-deep slimed stone sill with deep, flat pools immediately above and below it; a thirty-by-eight-pace dry gravel bar mid-river; the dead carter's cart at the far edge. Brom finds a lipped submerged stone four paces short of the bar by feel at noon. Seln counts seven from the top of the grass fall by where the water 'moves wrong'.

The gate-woman from Chapter 1 doubles as the steading's woman: she gives the carters' lore (dusk, out of the water, river's colour, the man who lit something buried in pieces, the second man's throat, the third not come up), boils water before the crew comes back up, binds all four, and gives the non-fighter's verdict; the bowman on the walk (Chapter 1) relays through her that nobody shouted. Both remain unnamed.

The plan's second mechanism: after the single lattice-point, Karis holds the pack's attention with sound — a river stone struck on her knife's pommel — using Chapter 1's loudest-sound observation; the pack's later adaptation is to abandon the silent bodies and converge on that sound.

The pack's first-mover behavior as Cael's on-page finding: the hounds do not follow a fixed leader but break toward whichever animal commits first, and the same big grey in the far channel has been the first mover each time because it decides fastest; Cael's burst supplies the first movement so that every dog, including the grey, turns — putting the grey's back to the downstream pool where Seln is. This stays inside the packet's 'pack geometry' allowance and does not add biology.

Seln's method left unstated: he goes into the river himself and rises out of the downstream pool behind the leader; whether his Shadow Path or fifteen years of craft made him unseen is not resolved on the page ('By then it doesn't matter what counts.'), preserving POV honesty and avoiding a new fact about the hounds' senses.

Weapons and small objects: Brom's bill-hook on a short haft (the fence-line tool from Chapter 1), knives for the rest, Karis's river stone; the crew's kill allocation — Seln two (the leader and one more in the far channel), Lira one on the bar, Brom one at his stone, Cael one at the bank; two lost to the current (one in the first exchange, one at the break).

Aftermath texture: the days at Thornwater compressed in summary (the carter carrying the slip and the recovered cart down; Seln checking the ford each dusk and reporting 'Nothing'; Karis dictating her notes to Cael because she cannot hold a pen and making him read them back twice, Pike's habit); Pike's copy returning by carter on the fourth day.
state_change_proposals: Timeline: the ford is cleared at dusk on the fifty-third day past the Line (Lowmarch board on the fiftieth; two days' walk; the ford walked at noon and fought at dusk on the fifty-third). The unit is at Thornwater's grain loft through at least the fifty-seventh day, when Pike's copied line arrives by carter. Cael is eighteen.

Cael: nine fragments + anomaly, unchanged. Deployment since the Line: ONE — a single Wind-adjacent burst, spent openly at the ford in front of the party, the steading's bowman on the gate-walk, and no other witness. Cost: breath, the locked landing beat (a hound reached him inside it), frameworks unsettled for about a day. Injury OPEN at chapter end: right calf bitten through (entry and exit wounds), washed and bound in boiled cloth by the steading's woman; no healer; walked on with a limp he catalogues; closing 'slower than he told anyone and faster than the woman said it would'. Shadow-adjacent unused; the seal restated in the log. Iron-adjacent read described only as wanting to run and held.

Brom: Iron Skin declared once at the ford and withdrawn; fought the rest without it. Injury OPEN: right forearm opened to the bone from wrist to mid-forearm by a hound's jaws, washed and bound tight by the steading's woman, ordered not to use it; unbound arm carries the hook. No healer.

Lira: no Wind used at the ford; fought and was fast without it (her Chapter 4 want is now seeded on the page). Injury OPEN: right ankle turned fully on the bar's gravel at speed, not broken, bound flat toes-to-shin, ordered off it three days then a stick; carried up the bank on Seln's shoulder.

Karis: lit exactly one lattice-point (the bait) and refused a second under attack. Injury OPEN: both palms cut across, deep and clean, by the edge of her own knife while holding it by the blade against a hound; bound to the fingers; cannot hold a pen — Cael is writing her notes at dictation. Her hypothesis (discharge-sense; water masks discharge; the ford is theirs because the river hides them) is now a confirmed finding in her notebook and the log.
Seln: uninjured. Counted the seven, stated the cut-dog geometry, went into the river unseen and killed the lead hound and one other. First honest employment continues; nothing said about his method.

Pike's ledger: the ford slip's HOLD, Teague struck through with one line and the five names entered beneath; the completion line entered and copied for the crew: 'Stillhound pack, Thornwater ford: cleared. Five confirmed. Crew of five, four injured, none lost. Price paid.' Forty marks paid by the hold (the hold also fed them). Wall-sheet position not moved on the page — reserved for Chapter 4 per the card.

Knowledge state: the party now knows, as a confirmed finding, that stillhounds hunt Path discharge, are nearly blind to still bodies, turn as one to the loudest declaration and otherwise to the loudest sound, lie hidden in water (which masks discharge), hunt at dusk, keep a cut-dog on the road, and break toward whichever hound moves first. Nobody has heard of quiet ground; no healer, no Tide practitioner, no Oryn has appeared (the woman's 'nearest walks a route and she's not due' is the only reference, unnamed, consistent with the architecture's Chapter 6 arrival).

Stillhound population at Thornwater's ford: five dead (bodies on the stones, confirmed by the steading's woman at the gate), two escaped downstream and unaccounted for; Cael logs the two as open, not as nothing.

Third-party verdicts on record: the steading's woman — 'You didn't know about that one.' and 'Four. Out of five. Two men went down to that ford this month and one came up.'; the bowman via her — none of them shouted; Pike's copied line as above. Cael's shelf of kept sentences now has three edge-territory entries (carter, bowman, Pike).

The first pass ran to 7,687 words and was cut by density only; every must_include beat, all four exchanges, every listed injury, the mid-aftermath seal line, and the mandated ending are intact. Further compression, if the editor wants the chapter nearer 4,600, is available in the ford catalogue and the loft dialogue without touching obligations.

The packet's outcome text says 'Nobody uninjured' and then lists four injuries; the ledger line it mandates says 'four injured'. The chapter follows the ledger line and the card: Seln is uninjured, and the woman, the log, Pike's line, and Cael's last sentence all count four of five.

Whether stillhounds can sense a suppression-type declaration is deliberately left unasserted to stay inside the invention budget (no new fact about their senses).

If the editor reads this as anticipating Oryn too early, the sentence can be cut to 'There's no healer here.' without other change.
